name: Wedding budget

seoDesc: Wedding budget: work out total (Ceremony) from number of guests and the bride's dress. A free finance calculator with the formula, units and a worked example.
summary: Supply number of guests, the bride's dress, the jewelery and the groom's suit and accessories and the Wedding budget calculator solves for total (Ceremony). It is built for a budget, a loan conversation, a payslip check or a what-if before you talk to a lender. Press Calculate for the answer; change a value and it steps off screen until you press again, so each edit can be judged on its own.

sections.title: How does the Wedding budget calculator work?
sections.html:
The Wedding budget calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports total (Ceremony) in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you type in number of guests, the bride's dress, the jewelery and the groom's suit and accessories.

The arithmetic runs locally each time an input changes. The page knows which values you have given it and which it still has to derive, so the results panel is never stale.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: The formula behind the Wedding budget calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

Total=-total − wedding budget balance − total + how much do you want to spend? − total − total
Wedding rings=total − bride's dress − groom's suit and accessories − hair and makeup − jewelery
Florist=-wedding stationery − photography & Video + total − wedding planner
Rehearsal dinner=-ceremony musicians ÷ DJs − wedding cake − catering − liquors + total − venue
Total=hotel + limo rental and transportation
Total=ceremony site + officiant

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Units are handled by conversion rather than by convention. Whatever chip you choose, the number is turned into a single base unit before the calculation and rendered back afterwards, so a form filled with a mixture of systems still gives the right answer.

Display rounding is separate from calculation rounding: the digits you see are shortened, the value behind them is not. Numbers far from everyday size are shown in scientific notation so the significant digits stay readable.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Wedding budget calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Comparing two offers that quote their costs in different ways
  • Building a monthly budget and testing how one number shifts the rest
  • Sizing up a purchase before you commit to it
  • Any time the same 4 figures keep coming back — number of guests, the bride's dress and the jewelery — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Change one input at a time when you are exploring. Two simultaneous changes make it impossible to tell which one moved the result.
  • If a result surprises you, look at the order of magnitude before the digits: a plausible number in the wrong unit looks more convincing than an implausible one, and is easier to miss.
  • Round only at the end. The calculator carries full precision internally, so re-entering a value you already rounded is the fastest way to introduce drift.
  • Write the answer down with its unit. A bare number copied into a report later is exactly where units get lost.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html: • Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.

faq.q: What does the Wedding budget calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns total (Ceremony), derived from number of guests, the bride's dress and the jewelery. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Wedding budget calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for number of guests, the bride's dress, the jewelery and the groom's suit and accessories, which is 26 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter how much do you want to spend? in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. How much do you want to spend? opens in US Dollar and the chip beside it offers 113 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

With the values the page starts from, the calculator reports Total = 0. Treat that as a reference point rather than a recommendation: it exists so you can tell at a glance whether your own inputs are on the same scale.

faq.q: Is the Wedding budget calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.
